evidence: Nestled along the ancient brick-paved streets of Bát Tràng, a village renowned for its centuries-old ceramic tradition, lies a series of pottery shops that serve as both commercial outlets and cultural museums. These shops, known locally as "Cửa hàng gốm Bát Tràng," are scattered throughout the village, each one a testament to the enduring legacy of Vietnamese ceramics that began during the Ly Dynasty.

Hand-painted handicrafts line the front of each shop, showcasing the intricate designs and skilled workmanship of the artisans who create them. The architectural style of these shops reflects the traditional Vietnamese aesthetic, with many featuring red brick courtyards and narrow, winding alleys that add to the charm of the village.
